newsitem.title: USA: NABL asks meeting with SEC's Hunt after criticisms.
newsitem.headline: NABL asks meeting with SEC's Hunt after criticisms.

text.p: Bond lawyers want to meet with SEC panelist Isaac Hunt to discuss his charges this week that lawyers lack leadership on political contributions and other front-burner regulatory issues affecting muni bonds, a spokesperson for lawyers said on Friday.
Amy Dunbar, chief lobbyist for the National Association of Bond Lawyers, discussed the NABL plan to meet with Hunt in a telephone interview on Friday with Reuters.
Hunt, who joined the SEC a year ago, told the Bond Club of Virginia on Wednesday that he is "troubled" that NABL has not taken aggressive steps to curb "pay-to-play" by members.
Pay-to-play refers to bond professionals that give political contributions to elected municipal clients in return for bond business.
Hunt also said bond lawyers are failing to tell clients up front in "retainer" agreements whether they will help protect them from securities law violations.
He cited stinging remarks by U.S. District Judge William Yoer Mark Ferber, who was convicted on graft and kickback charges involving bond deals.
